subject: chemistry
title: Redox Processes Adventure 2: Voltaic and electrolytic cells
welcome_lead: Today you'll build a voltaic cell — and electrolyse molten salt.
meta_desc: Chemistry — voltaic cells, electrode potentials, electrolysis, electroplating.
final_note: You learned voltaic cells turn chemistry into electricity (anode oxidation, cathode reduction); electrolytic cells use electricity to drive non-spontaneous redox.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Daniell cell: Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(aq) || Cu²⁺(aq) | Cu(s).

Zn anode: Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻ (oxidation, negative).
Cu cathode: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu (reduction, positive).
Electrons flow Zn → Cu through wire; ions flow through salt bridge.

E° cell = E° cathode − E° anode = 0.34 − (-0.76) = +1.10 V.

E° measured vs standard hydrogen electrode (E° = 0 V).

More positive E° → species more easily reduced (stronger oxidising agent).

- F₂/F⁻: +2.87 V (very strong oxidiser).
- Cu²⁺/Cu: +0.34 V.
- Zn²⁺/Zn: -0.76 V.
- Li⁺/Li: -3.04 V (very strong reducing agent).

Electricity forces non-spontaneous redox. Anode +; cathode -.

Molten NaCl: Na⁺ → Na at cathode; 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻ at anode (chlor-alkali process — global industry).

Aqueous NaCl: at cathode, H₂O reduced (H₂ released, not Na, since H₂O more easily reduced).

Quantitative: Q = It, charge per mole electrons = F = 96,500 C/mol (Faraday's constant).

mcqs.q: In a voltaic cell, the anode is:
If E°cell for a redox reaction is positive, what does that tell you?
options: A positive E°cell guarantees the reaction will happen rapidly at room temperature.
The reaction is thermodynamically feasible — but it may still be very slow if kinetic barriers are high.
The salt bridge prevents the solutions from reacting with each other.
A positive E°cell means the reaction is exothermic in every case.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a salt bridge in an electrochemical cell?
options: A positive E°cell means the reaction is exothermic in every case.
It completes the circuit by allowing ions to flow between the half-cells, maintaining electrical neutrality.
The salt bridge carries electrons between the two electrodes.
The salt bridge prevents the solutions from reacting with each other.

mcqs.q: Can a single standard electrode potential be measured in isolation?
options: A positive E°cell means the reaction is exothermic in every case.
Each electrode has an absolute potential that can be measured directly with a voltmeter.
Standard electrode potentials are measured by submerging the electrode in pure water.
No — electrode potentials are RELATIVE values measured against a reference (the standard hydrogen electrode, defined as 0 V).
